profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a university software engineering research lab between the analytics workstream and the infrastructure workstream for a study on gender influence in student teams' online communication during an eight-week GitHub-based course project. The team is preparing the final integration step before analysis begins: the analytics side needs a clean weekly communication dataset joined with team composition and learning-gain measures, while the infrastructure side is responsible for exporting Slack and GitHub data from the course systems and placing it in the shared research repository. The agenda is to align on the handoff format, what counts as the 'final' export, ownership of the merged dataset, and the expected status by Friday. The expected outcome is apparent agreement that Priya will receive the final dataset package and start analysis next week, while Evan will finish the export and publish the shared artifacts.

members.name: Priya Natarajan
members.role: Research Software Engineer for Learning Analytics
members.expertise: Python data pipelines, educational data analysis, statistical preprocessing, mixed-methods coding workflows
members.background: Priya supports empirical software engineering studies and usually works downstream from raw platform exports, turning them into analysis-ready longitudinal datasets for faculty and PhD students.
members.private_state: Priya wants to begin modeling immediately next week and is trying to avoid another round of manual cleaning; she is especially concerned about preserving week-by-week team communication structure and not having to chase missing metadata after the handoff.
hidden_assumptions: A 'final export' means a frozen, analysis-ready package with stable schemas and all identifiers already reconciled across Slack, GitHub, roster, and survey files.

Weekly communication data should be aligned to the course's teaching weeks, Monday through Sunday in local campus time, because that is how the learning-gain measures and assignment cadence were defined.
The shared 'team dataset' includes both student message records and derived participant/team attributes needed for modeling, not just the raw communication logs.
If a dataset is placed in the shared research repository, the infrastructure side still owns any late data-fix requests because they are the source-of-truth maintainers.

members.name: Evan Morales
members.expertise: API integrations, LMS and Slack exports, GitHub event collection, research data warehousing, access-controlled storage
members.background: Evan maintains the lab's connectors to course platforms and usually delivers standardized exports into the central warehouse, leaving study-specific transformations to analysts.
members.private_state: Evan wants to close out the data extraction task this week and avoid committing his team to custom transformations or ongoing support once the files are posted.
hidden_assumptions: A 'final export' means the last raw pull from source systems for this study window, not a cleaned or fully merged analysis dataset.
Weekly bucketing should follow the warehouse default of rolling seven-day UTC windows starting from the first captured event, because that is how their export jobs are configured.
The 'team dataset' refers to the Slack/GitHub event tables associated with each project team; survey and roster joins are downstream enrichment owned by analytics.
Once the package is published to the shared research repository, ownership effectively transfers to the analytics side unless there is a system outage or missing source file.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Evan will deliver the 'final export' by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya hears 'final export' as a frozen, analysis-ready dataset package with normalized user IDs, joined roster/survey metadata, and no further schema changes expected.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan means the last raw extraction from Slack and GitHub for the study period, with standard warehouse tables and only minimal formatting cleanup.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research software coordination, 'final export' is a familiar phrase that sounds routine; both assume the other uses their local team's convention, and the discussion naturally focuses on timing rather than the level of processing.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the team dataset
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss putting the 'team dataset' in the shared repo so Priya can start analysis.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya assumes the team dataset includes communication events plus team composition, gender labels, pre/post understanding scores, and week numbers ready for modeling.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan assumes the team dataset only covers team-linked platform activity data from Slack and GitHub, excluding survey-derived and manually curated demographic fields.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'team dataset' sounds naturally broad enough to both parties, and because each person's omitted pieces are standard in their own workflow, neither sees a reason to enumerate what is inside.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on getting the communication data 'broken out by week' for the eight-week project.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya expects weeks to map to the course calendar in local campus time, Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59, matching assignments and survey timing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan plans to use the existing ETL job's seven-day UTC buckets anchored on the first event ingestion timestamp for the workspace.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both sincerely believe 'by week' has an obvious implementation, and week bucketing feels like a minor technical detail rather than a design choice worth surfacing in a short coordination meeting.

misalignment_points.topic: Ownership after publishing to the shared repo
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that once the package is in the shared research repo, Priya can take it from there.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya presupposes she can proceed with analysis while still relying on Evan's team to patch identifier mismatches or add omitted fields discovered during validation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Evan presupposes that publication to the shared repo marks the handoff boundary, after which analytics owns any study-specific corrections or merges.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'take it from there' conventionally signals smooth progress, and both interpret it through their usual division of labor without explicitly discussing post-handoff support obligations.

When Evan says the final export, I'm expecting the frozen, analysis-ready package: reconciled IDs across Slack, GitHub, roster, and surveys, stable schema, and everything needed to run the week-level team models. If that lands by Friday, I can spend the weekend validating instead of chasing missing metadata.
